articles.title: TrailWhistle: A Bird-Call Identifier That Works With Zero Bars of Signal
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass Last spring I was on a trail at dawn, that electric half-hour when every bird in the forest is shouting at once,…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass What I Built Last spring I was on a trail at dawn, that electric half-hour when every bird in the forest is shouting at once, and I realized I could name maybe three of them. My phone had no signal, and the bird apps I knew about needed the cloud. So I just stood there, surrounded by a symphony I couldn't understand. That frustration became TrailWhistle : point your phone at the dawn chorus and it tells you who's singing, using AI that runs entirely on your device. It listens to 3 seconds of birdsong and identifies the species, with common name, scientific name, and confidence score. No internet. No account. No data leaving your phone. It's also a small biodiversity survey tool.
articles.author: Sourabh Kumar

articles.title: Touch Grass Go: Turning Real-World Nature Adventures into an RPG
articles.excerpt: We sit for hours on end in front of screens, switching between tabs, scrolling down feeds, and playing games. But what if we could harness that same determination that gets us to play games to get us…
articles.body: We sit for hours on end in front of screens, switching between tabs, scrolling down feeds, and playing games. But what if we could harness that same determination that gets us to play games to get us to explore the world around us? This thought process gave birth to Touch Grass Go , an android app, that turns real-world exploring into an RPG nature quest. The Idea What if real life had quests, experience points, levels, and daily streaks? With Touch Grass Go, your next adventure could be as simple as observing birds in your neighborhood, practicing mindfulness outdoors, or discovering interesting leaves along your walk. The goal is simple: make exploring nature engaging while encouraging users to spend less time staring at their screens.
articles.author: Aditya Alibade

articles.title: Java Variables, Data Types and Type Casting: A Simple Guide with Examples
articles.excerpt: Every program needs to remember things: a user's age, a price, a name, a yes/no answer. In Java, you do this with variables. But Java is strict. Before you store anything, you have to say what kind of…
articles.body: Every program needs to remember things: a user's age, a price, a name, a yes/no answer. In Java, you do this with variables . But Java is strict. Before you store anything, you have to say what kind of thing it is. That strictness confused me at first. Why can't I just put a decimal number into an int ? Why does byte c = a + b give an error? In this post, we'll go through all of this step by step, with small examples you can run yourself. What is a variable? A variable is a named box in memory that holds a value. To make one, you write the type , then the name , then (optionally) the value .

articles.title: ErrandQuest — Touch Grass and Get Every Errand Done in One Trip
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass What I Built The Problem Most digital to-do apps keep people glued to screens—organizing, tagging, and rearrangi…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass What I Built ** ErrandQuest** is an open-source, AI-powered errand planner designed with one core philosophy: make the screen the shortest part of your day so you can get outside and touch grass. The Problem Most digital to-do apps keep people glued to screens—organizing, tagging, and rearranging lists—yet fail to solve real-world friction: Which errands can be combined into a single stop? What order should I visit shops in so I don't drive or walk in circles? What essential items must I pack before stepping out the door? Why did I buy ice cream first, only to have it melt while visiting the print shop? As a result, people make 3 or 4 separate trips throughout the day, repeatedly opening their phones.

articles.title: Java if, switch and Loops: Which One Should You Use?
articles.excerpt: Java Decisions and Loops: if, switch, while, do-while, for and the Enhanced for Up to now, our Java programs ran from top to bottom, one line after another. Real programs aren't like that. They need t…
articles.body: Java Decisions and Loops: if, switch, while, do-while, for and the Enhanced for Up to now, our Java programs ran from top to bottom, one line after another. Real programs aren't like that. They need to make choices ("is the user logged in?") and repeat things ("check every item in the cart"). Java gives us two groups of tools for this: Conditionals help the program decide: if , else if , else , and switch . Loops help the program repeat: while , do-while , for , and the enhanced for . Let's go through each one, and I'll also share when to pick which, because that's the part tutorials often skip. articles.title: OOP in Java: What Really Happens Behind the Scenes
articles.excerpt: When I first learned OOP in Java, I could repeat the four pillars like a poem: encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction. But if you had asked me what actually happens in memory when I wri…
articles.body: When I first learned OOP in Java, I could repeat the four pillars like a poem: encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction. But if you had asked me what actually happens in memory when I write new Dog() , I would have gone quiet. That gap is what confused me most. I knew the words, but not the machine behind them. And without that picture, things like "why did changing one object change another?" or "how does Java know which method to call?" felt like magic. In this post, we'll learn each OOP idea and then peek behind the curtain to see what the JVM does. If you've read my post on JDK, JRE and JVM, this is a nice follow-up, because the JVM is the star here too. First, a quick picture of memory Before any OOP, you need a simple map of where things live.

articles.body: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested an executive at a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently relieved the FBI of sensitive data on thousands of agents, multiple sources tell KrebsOnSecurity. The New York Times reported today that the FBI has arrested a Canadian man in Pennsylvania on suspicion of assisting ShinyHunters. The Times story did not identify the man, nor did a statement on Twitter/X about the arrest from FBI Director Kash Patel .

articles.body: Credit: NASA NASA is advancing American leadership in space by taking the next step toward a future where commercial space stations lead the way in low Earth orbit. On Friday, the agency released its final Request for Proposals inviting industry to submit plans for the next generation of commercial space stations. “In alignment with the President’s National Space Policy, NASA is committed to maintaining a sustained American presence in low Earth orbit long after the International Space Station retires,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “We will continue to need a place to conduct research, develop technologies, train crews, and prepare for missions to the Moon and Mars.

articles.title: NASA Demonstrates Next-Generation Heat Shield Technologies
articles.excerpt: NASA is testing heat shields that can keep astronauts safe as they return from missions to the Moon and Mars in an unusual way: by taking out the trash. When Northrop Grumman 24th cargo resupply missi…
articles.body: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) A KREPE-3 capsule floats inside the Northrup Grumman Cygnus XL 24 cargo spacecraft on October 7. Inside the capsule is a 3-D printed heat shield designed by researchers at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. NASA NASA is testing heat shields that can keep astronauts safe as they return from missions to the Moon and Mars in an unusual way: by taking out the trash. When Northrop Grumman 24 th cargo resupply mission for NASA undocked from the International Space Station, it carried a fleet of 12 small, experimental capsules designed to test the next generation of thermal protection materials that could serve as the foundation for future heat shields.
